about: The roadmap of the port. The plan thread owns the phases and their order. To pick the next step: the first planned step whose earlier steps in the same phase it needs are done. `done_when` is the test a step must pass; `components` names rows of docs/devlog/data/the_port_plan/components.json. The pull request that starts, ships or replans a step edits this file. `owner` is the thread that has claimed a step: claim a step by writing your thread's title there, in a pull request, before you start.

milestones.title: Format parity
milestones.proof: gleam-in-nim format prints byte for byte what gleam format prints, on the 918 upstream formatter tests, on gleam_stdlib and on the corpus.

milestones.title: Check parity
milestones.proof: Same errors and warnings as the reference on the upstream type checker tests; same package interface JSON as gleam export package-interface on gleam_stdlib and the corpus.

milestones.title: The standard library compiles to Erlang
milestones.proof: compile-package --target erlang --no-beam gives byte identical .erl and .hrl files for gleam_stdlib and the corpus; the 483 upstream Erlang snapshots reproduce.

milestones.title: It runs on the BEAM
milestones.proof: In CI, with Erlang/OTP installed, the output of the port passes upstream's test/language suite and gleam_stdlib's own tests.

milestones.title: JavaScript parity
milestones.proof: Byte identical .mjs and .d.mts for gleam_stdlib and the corpus; the 843 upstream JavaScript snapshots reproduce; test/language passes on Node.

milestones.title: A real build tool
milestones.proof: gleam-in-nim new, add, build, test and run work on a fresh project with Hex dependencies, with no reference binary involved.

milestones.title: Port complete
milestones.proof: Every row of the coverage map is verified or listed as an intentional divergence; the language server answers an editor.

phases.title: Before the first line
phases.goal: Know what is being ported, where it comes from, how others did such a thing, and how this project will work. Every step is an explainer.

steps.title: The workflow and the repo
steps.what: How Pietro has been working with nimib and AI, and this site made accordingly: devlog, review mode, the look, roadmap, coverage map, CI.

steps.title: Gleam, its people and its programs
steps.what: The language, how it is used, the projects big and small, the people, and the house rules a port should respect.

steps.title: Where Gleam's decisions live
steps.what: No specification and no RFCs: a ranked map of where design decisions are written down, and a recipe to look one up.

steps.title: A corpus of real Gleam
steps.what: Seventy five projects pinned at exact commits with their licences (corpus/corpus.json), and the tool that pins, fetches and measures them.

steps.title: The BEAM and Erlang
steps.what: A short history, what it solves, how a language is built on it, how Gleam lives on it.

steps.title: Elm, the other root
steps.what: Its history and principles, the type system, developer experience, and what Gleam took from it.

steps.title: The compiler, taken apart
steps.what: How compilers are made and how Gleam's is: the pipeline, the components and their sizes, its history, and how it compares with other compilers.

steps.title: The port plan
steps.what: Scope, the order of work, which backend first, the milestones, how each step is verified, and this roadmap.

steps.title: Other rewrites
steps.what: How a big project is rewritten in another language, by people and by AI: what worked, what did not, what to copy.

steps.title: How to develop
steps.what: Specs, decision records, tooling to verify the port and tooling for Pietro to review it.

steps.title: Harvest the upstream Rust tests
steps.what: Many upstream tests keep inputs and expected values in Rust macros, not in snapshot files: 918 formatter assertions, 374 inference assertions, lexer and parser assertions, dependency modules of backend tests. Extract them to JSON test vectors.
steps.done_when: Every upstream assertion macro call is available as data, with counts per component in the coverage map.

steps.title: What the real compiler says
steps.what: The reference compiler run over every package of the corpus, for Erlang and for JavaScript: abstract forms, Erlang source, JavaScript, package interface and diagnostics kept as expected results (corpus/golden.json, tools/golden.nim).
steps.done_when: Every corpus package has a recorded reference result for both targets, with hashes; a second run of a sample gives the same hashes; tools/golden.nim list feeds tools/difftest.nim.
steps.owner: Research Gleam, its community and corpus

steps.title: Erlang in CI
steps.what: Add Erlang/OTP, Node and the reference binary to CI so compiled output can be executed.
steps.done_when: CI can run erlc and escript; a smoke test compiles and runs reference output.
steps.owner: Research Gleam, its community and corpus
